questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A teenager was riding a bicycle when she saw a classmate walking toward her. The teenager rode quickly toward the classmate, knowing that he would think she would run into him on her current trajectory. The teenager was not purposefully trying to harm or touch him. The classmate saw the teenager riding toward him and yelled at her to stop. The teenager swerved at the last moment and avoided hitting him. The classmate had a panic attack because he thought that the teenager would hit him.
Is the classmate likely to succeed if he sues the teenager for assault?

choices.A: No, because the teenager did not make contact with the classmate.
choices.B: No, because the teenager did not purposefully try to harm or touch the classmate.
choices.C: Yes, because the teenager acted with the requisite intent.
choices.D: Yes, because the teenager's conduct was extreme and outrageous.

questions.explanation:
Two types of intent
Purpose Girl desires to hit Boy A
Knowledge Girl is substantially certain she will also hit Boy B

Assault occurs when (1) a defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and (2) the defendant's affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact. The intent requirement is met when the defendant acts with either:

  • purpose - the desire to cause anticipation of an imminent harmful or offensive contact or
  • knowledge - the substantial certainty that the plaintiff will suffer such anticipation.

Here, the teenager rode her bicycle directly at her classmate, causing him to think that she would hit him (anticipation of imminent contact). And since the teenager acted with substantial certainty that the classmate would think she would run into him, she acted with the requisite intent. As a result, the classmate is likely to succeed in a suit against the teenager for assault.

(Choice A) Assault merely requires that the plaintiff be placed in anticipation of imminent contact. Actual bodily contact is not required. Therefore, the fact that the teenager did not make contact with the classmate is irrelevant.

(Choice B) The intent to make contact with the plaintiff is a requirement for battery, but assault merely requires the intent to cause the plaintiff to anticipate imminent contact. Therefore, the fact that the teenager did not purposefully try to harm or touch the classmate does not absolve her of liability for assault.

(Choice D) Extreme and outrageous conduct (i.e., conduct that is unacceptable in civilized society) is an element of intentional infliction of emotional distress--not assault, which only requires intentional conduct.

📌 Educational Objective

For assault, intent exists when a defendant acts with the purpose (desire) or knowledge (substantial certainty) that his/her conduct will cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (providing the elements for assault).
questions.zh-question:
主题：侵权法（Torts）— 故意侵权（Intentional Torts）

题目：
一名青少年骑自行车时看见一名同学朝她走来。该青少年迅速朝同学骑去，她知道同学会以为她会按当前路线撞上他。该青少年并不是有意要伤害或接触他。同学看见青少年朝自己骑来，便大喊让她停下。青少年在最后一刻转向，避免撞到他。由于同学以为青少年会撞到他，他发生了惊恐发作（panic attack）。
如果同学以 assault 起诉这名青少年，他是否很可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为青少年没有与该同学发生接触（contact）。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为青少年并非有意要伤害或接触该同学。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为青少年具备了所要求的 intent（故意）。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为青少年的行为是极端且令人震惊的（extreme and outrageous）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Intentional Torts - Harm to persons

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：殴打（assault） 的 intent 只要有“想让对方害怕”或“明知对方会害怕”的一种就够，不需要真的撞上人。

三秒认题路径：

先看 assault → 再看 intent → substantial certainty → 能上诉？不是 → 选 C

核心法律规则

殴打（assault） 的核心，是被告做了会让原告立刻担心马上被碰到、而且是有害或冒犯性接触的行为。意图（intent） 不只包括“就是想吓你”，也包括明知自己的行为会让对方几乎必然产生这种恐惧。考场上你只要抓住：purpose 或 knowledge，二选一满足就够。这里被告骑车直冲同学，题干还明说她知道对方会以为自己要撞上去，所以 intent 成立。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts, Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 — 这条把 assault 的 intent 锁定为 purpose 或 substantial certainty。

思维导图

题眼：她有没有让同学“马上会被撞到”的恐惧？
YES 线： 骑车直冲 → 原告立刻躲避 → anticipation of imminent contact
intent 关卡： purpose 或 knowledge / substantial certainty
卡死点：不需要真的撞到人；“最后一刻躲开”不救被告。
结论： assault 成立 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她没真的撞到，也没“故意打人”，那就不算 assault。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有故意让对方 担心马上被碰到（anticipation of imminent contact）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的接触到底有没有发生」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 知道同学会以为她要撞上去，这正好满足 assault 的 knowledge 型 intent，所以原告可胜诉。

❌ 事实误判 | 接触条件偷换

✕ A: 误把 contact 当必要条件，assault 不要求真碰到。

❌ 概念混淆 | battery 意图混用

✕ B: 把“故意碰人”当 assault 标准，错把 touch 的要求搬进来了。

❌ 法律适用 | IIED 要件误套

✕ D: 把 extreme and outrageous 套到 assault，上错规则了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否让对方立刻害怕被碰到”，再看 intent 是 purpose 还是 substantial certainty。

考场速记

记忆口诀： assault 看“怕不怕被马上碰到”，不是看“最后有没有真碰到”。

遇到 assault（殴打），先问：被告是不是想让对方害怕，或者明知对方一定会害怕；答是，就别被“没接触”骗走。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Apply assault intent not battery elements

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A farmer kept antiques in an uninhabited farmhouse on his property. The farmhouse had been broken into several times in the past, and some of the farmer's goods had been stolen. Instead of posting "No Trespassing" signs, the farmer decided to install an alarm system to deter intruders. While the farmer was in the farmhouse installing the alarm system, he heard a window open in the adjoining room. The farmer crept very quietly to the door of the room, threw the door open, and found a 10-year-old intruder. The farmer immediately struck the child very hard in the face, breaking her nose.
In an action on behalf of the child against the farmer to recover for the injury to her nose, is the child likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the farmer did not use deadly force.
choices.B: No, because the farmer had probable cause to believe that the child was a thief.
choices.C: Yes, because the farmer should have posted a "No Trespassing" sign.
choices.D: Yes, because the farmer used excessive force.

questions.explanation:
©UWorld

In defending against a plaintiff's action to recover damages for an intentionally inflicted injury (e.g., battery claim), a defendant can argue that he/she was privileged to use force to prevent the plaintiff's imminent intrusion on the defendant's land or personal property. This privilege applies when:

  • the plaintiff's imminent intrusion is not privileged
  • the defendant first asks the plaintiff to desist and the plaintiff disregards the request*
  • the defendant reasonably believes that the plaintiff is intruding or imminently will intrude upon the defendant's property and that the intrusion can be prevented or terminated only by the means used
  • the means used are reasonably proportionate to the value of the interest the defendant is protecting—i.e., the defendant cannot use excessive force and
  • the means used are not intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily injury.

Here, the child's entrance on the farmer's property was unprivileged because she did not have the farmer's permission to enter. This entitled the farmer to use reasonable force to remove her from his farmhouse (e.g., by carrying her off his property). Instead, the farmer used excessive force because he struck the girl very hard in the face and broke her nose. Therefore, the child will likely prevail in an action to recover for the injury to her nose.

*The defendant need not ask the plaintiff to desist if the defendant reasonably believes that (1) a request will be useless or dangerous or (2) substantial harm will be done before the request can be made.

(Choice A) Although the farmer striking the girl very hard in the face was not deadly force, it was excessive force.

(Choice B) Even if the farmer had probable cause to believe that the child was a thief, he was only privileged to use reasonable force to protect his property (not seen here).

(Choice C) A defendant need not have posted "No Trespassing" signs to defend his/her property.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant who uses force to prevent a plaintiff's imminent intrusion on the defendant's land or personal property can only use means that are reasonably proportionate to the value of the interest the defendant is protecting—i.e., the defendant cannot use excessive force.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 30 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 6, 2021) (setting forth the requirements for a defendant's use of force to defend property).
questions.zh-question:
一名农夫将古董存放在其地产上一座无人居住的农舍里。该农舍过去曾被多次闯入，农夫的一些财物被盗。农夫没有张贴“禁止非法侵入”的标志，而是决定安装一个警报系统来威慑入侵者。当农夫在农舍里安装警报系统时，他听到隔壁房间有窗户打开的声音。农夫悄悄地爬到房间门口，猛地推开门，发现一个10岁的入侵者。农夫立即猛击孩子的脸部，打断了她的鼻子。

在一场代表该儿童向农夫提起的、就其鼻子受伤要求赔偿的诉讼中，该儿童是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为农夫没有使用致命武力。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为农夫有合理理由相信该儿童是小偷。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为农夫本应张贴“禁止非法侵入”的标志。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为农夫使用了过度武力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Intentional Torts - Defense of property

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：防卫财产时，能不能因为对方是侵入者，就对其使用超过合理必要范围的武力。

三秒认题路径：

侵入财产 → 能否防卫 → 只限合理力 → 打脸致鼻折 → 过度用力 → 选 D

核心法律规则

防卫财产（defense of property）的考场意思：你可以用合理武力阻止或终止对自己土地、房屋或动产的即将发生的侵入（imminent intrusion），但不能上来就下重手。

合理武力（reasonable force）的考场意思：只够把人赶走、拦住、制止即可；如果升级到严重伤害风险，通常就越线了。

过度武力（excessive force）的考场意思：即使对方是擅自闯入，也不能用明显超出保护财产所需的打击方式。

核心判例：Restatement (Third) of Torts § 30 的规则锁定本题结论：防卫财产只能用与财产价值相称的合理武力，不能使用过度武力。

思维导图

题干先看：小孩是否是未获许可的进入者？
是：农场主可以防卫财产，但只能用合理武力（reasonable force）把她赶走。
再看：他是把人带离，还是直接对脸部重击？
直接重击并打断鼻梁 → 超出合理必要范围 → 过度武力成立
结论：能防卫，不等于能重伤；所以答案是 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方是偷闯进来的，还在屋里乱跑，农场主是不是可以狠狠干回去。

但考试真正问的是：他有没有资格把人赶走，而不是能不能借机打成受伤。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题最容易被deadly force带偏：A 选项把“不是致命武力”当成安全线，但本题的卡点是“是否过度”，不是“是否致死”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干中小孩只是未获许可进入，农场主最多只能用合理武力把她赶走；他却直接重击面部并打断鼻子，属于过度武力。

❌ 概念混淆 | 致命武力误判

✕ A: 只盯着deadly force，忽略“非致命也可能过度”。

❌ 法律适用 | 盗窃动机误判

✕ B: 就算怀疑她偷东西，也只能用合理武力赶人。

❌ 事实误判 | 标牌条件误判

✕ C: No Trespassing 不是防卫财产的前提条件。

这题建议用什么方法？

先确认是否存在未获许可侵入，再直接检查用力是否超过“赶走所需”的范围。

考场速记

记住一句：防卫财产只能“赶走”，不能“打狠”。看到侵入者先问合理武力，若出现重击、骨折、严重伤害，优先想到过度武力。

reason.en: Establishes the setting for the property-defense privilege.
reason.zh: 确立适用财产防卫特权的情境。

reason.en: Explains the farmer's security concerns but does not justify excessive force.
reason.zh: 说明农夫的安全顾虑，但不证明可使用过度武力。

reason.en: The intruder's age and status affect the proportionality of defensive force.
reason.zh: 侵入者的年龄与身份影响防卫武力的相当性。

keywords.text: struck the child very hard in the face

reason.en: Shows intentional harmful contact beyond what property defense permits.
reason.zh: 显示故意有害接触，超出财产防卫所允许的限度。

reason.en: Demonstrates that the force used was disproportionate to protecting property.
reason.zh: 表明所用武力与保护财产的利益不相称。

keywords.text: recover for the injury to her nose

reason.en: Frames the claim as recovery for intentionally inflicted personal injury.
reason.zh: 将请求框定为故意造成人身伤害的损害赔偿。

reason.en: Misleads by focusing only on the deadly-force ban, not overall reasonableness.
reason.zh: 仅聚焦禁止致命武力，忽略整体合理性标准。

reason.en: Imports a criminal-law standard irrelevant to civil property-defense force limits.
reason.zh: 引入与民事财产防卫武力限度无关的刑法标准。

reason.en: Suggests suspicion of theft alone authorizes harmful force.
reason.zh: 暗示仅怀疑盗窃即可授权使用有害武力。

reason.en: Implies posting signs is required to invoke the property-defense privilege.
reason.zh: 暗示必须张贴标示才能主张财产防卫特权。

reason.en: States the correct limit: force must be reasonably proportionate to the protected interest.
reason.zh: 指出正确界限：武力须与所保护利益合理相称。

highlights.text: found a 10-year-old intruder

reason.en: The intruder's identity limits how much force may be used to defend property.
reason.zh: 侵入者身份限制防卫财产可使用的武力程度。

highlights.text: struck the child very hard in the face, breaking her nose

reason.en: This conduct exceeds reasonable force and defeats the property-defense privilege.
reason.zh: 该行为超出合理武力，使财产防卫特权不成立。

highlights.text: is the child likely to prevail?

reason.en: Asks whether the farmer's privilege to defend property bars recovery.
reason.zh: 询问农夫的财产防卫特权是否阻却赔偿。

highlights.text: installing the alarm system

reason.en: Shows the farmer was lawfully on the premises, so defense was against an unprivileged intrusion.
reason.zh: 表明农夫合法在场，故针对的是无特权侵入。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A basketball player suffered an injury while participating in an impromptu basketball game at a public park. The injury occurred when the player and an opponent each tried to rebound the ball after a missed shot at the basket. During that encounter, the opponent swung his elbow to strike the player in his stomach to prevent him from getting the ball and injured him. The player now seeks compensation from the opponent.
At the trial, evidence was introduced tending to prove that the game had been rough from the beginning, that elbows and knees had frequently been used to discourage interference by opposing players, and that the player had been one of those making liberal use of such tactics.
In an action by the player against the opponent for battery, will the player likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the opponent did not intend to injure the player.
choices.B: No, because the player consented to the rough play.
choices.C: Yes, because the opponent caused contact with the player.
choices.D: Yes, because the opponent intended to strike the player with his elbow.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Scope of apparent consent
A and B play on opposing teams in a football game.
Same conduct A tackles B
Substantially similar conduct A tackles B offside
Conduct exceeds scope A punches B
↓
consent
↓
no consent
↓
no consentExplanation
Scope of apparent consent
A and B play on opposing teams in a football game.

Same conduct

A tackles B

Substantially similar conduct

A tackles B offside

Conduct exceeds scope

A punches B

consent            no consent

Battery occurs when a defendant intended to cause contact with the plaintiff's person, the defendant's affirmatively contact caused such contact, and that contact caused bodily harm or was offensive to the plaintiff. However, consent (actual, apparent, presumed, or emergency) is a defense to battery. And a plaintiff's participation in an athletic activity (e.g., basketball) may amount to apparent or presumed consent—especially if:

  • the defendant's conduct does not violate a safety rule of the sport
  • the conduct typically occurs during the activity and/or
  • the conduct does not involve significant risk of very serious injury or death.

Here, the opponent caused harmful contact with the player by intentionally striking him with his elbow (Choices C & D). The opponent's conduct violated a safety rule of the sport of basketball. But such rough play was typical in this game because the participants—including the player—had frequently used their elbows and knees. And elbowing a person in the stomach does not pose a risk of serious injury or death. Therefore, the player consented to the rough play, and the opponent is not liable for battery.

(Choice A) Although the opponent did not intend to injure the player, he still committed a battery because he intended to cause contact with the player. However, the player consented to such contact by participating in the game.

📌 Educational Objective

A plaintiff's participation in an athletic activity may amount to apparent or presumed consent to battery—especially if (1) the defendant's conduct does not violate a safety rule of the sport, (2) the conduct typically occurs during the activity, and/or (3) the conduct does not involve significant risk of very serious injury or death.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons §§ 101–104 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (providing an overview of the tort of battery).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 16 cmt. f (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (explaining the factors in considering whether participation in an athletic activity amounts to apparent or presumed consent).
questions.zh-question:
科目：侵权法（Torts）——故意侵权（Intentional Torts）

问题：
一名篮球运动员在公共公园参加一场临时组织的篮球比赛时受了伤。该伤害发生在该运动员和一名对手都试图在一次投篮不中后争抢篮板球时。在那次对抗中，对手挥肘击向该运动员的腹部，以阻止其抢球，并致其受伤。该运动员现在向该对手请求赔偿。
在审判中，证据表明比赛从一开始就十分粗野，双方经常使用肘部和膝部来阻止对方球员的干扰，而且该运动员本人也曾大量使用这种战术。
在该运动员以 battery 诉该对手的诉讼中，该运动员是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该对手并无意图使该运动员受伤。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该运动员已同意这种粗野的比赛方式。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该对手与该运动员发生了接触。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该对手意图用肘部击打该运动员。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Intentional Torts - Torts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：电池（battery）里，参加激烈球赛时的明示/默示同意（apparent or presumed consent）能不能挡掉原本成立的故意接触。

三秒认题路径：

球赛受伤 → 故意接触 → 看同意 → 触球常见 → 选 B

核心法律规则

只看这道题要用的规则

电池（battery）要求被告故意造成接触，而且这个接触导致人身伤害或冒犯性接触；但同意（consent）是抗辩。考场意思：就算有接触，只要原告已经同意这种接触，被告就不承担 battery 责任。

参加体育活动（athletic activity）时，原告常会对比赛中的正常或类似动作形成默示同意（implied consent）。考场意思：如果动作通常会在比赛里出现、没有严重危险、也不明显违背安全规则，原告就很难说“我完全没同意”。

这题里对方用肘部去抢球，虽然有意接触，但题干又说比赛一开始就很粗野，大家一直用肘和膝，而且这一动作不太会带来极严重伤害。考场意思：原告既然跟着这类粗暴打法上场，就已经把这种接触算进同意范围了。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 16 cmt. f 的思路就是：看体育活动中的接触是否落在比赛通常范围内，而不是只盯着“对方有没有故意碰到你”。

思维导图

先问：这是 battery 吗？
1.故意接触：对方确实用肘去撞人。
2.再问抗辩：原告有没有同意这种接触？
参加篮球这类对抗赛时，是否已有默示同意？
看三个信号：
· 动作是否常见于比赛
· 是否明显违反安全规则
· 是否带来极严重伤亡风险
本题卡死点：肘击在这场比赛里很常见，且不属严重危险动作，所以“同意”成立。
结论：虽然有故意接触，但原告已默示同意 → 不成立赔偿。
答案：B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方明明是intentionally strike，所以 battery 肯定赢。

但考试真正问的是：原告在这种粗野球赛里，有没有把这类接触一起同意进去。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“受伤很明显”带偏；只要接触落在比赛通常范围内，且不超出安全边界，原告就会输在 consent 这一关。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干显示比赛一直很粗野、大家常用肘膝，原告自己也参与这种打法；这正好说明他对这类接触已默示同意，所以 battery 不能成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 意图伤害误判

✕ A: 只盯着intend to injure，把“想不想伤人”当成关键点了。

❌ 事实误判 | 接触即胜误判

✕ C: 看到有caused contact就直接赢，漏掉了同意抗辩。

❌ 法律适用 | 故意要件误判

✕ D: 只证明intended to strike，还不够挡住 consent。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出“体育活动中的默示同意”这条抗辩，再看动作是否属于比赛常见接触。

考场速记

记住一句：球场粗碰先问同意，不是先问有没有受伤。

这类题的口令就是：rough play + common conduct + no serious risk = consent。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
While a woman was riding her horse on what she thought was a public path, the owner of a house next to the path approached her while shaking a stick and shouting, "Get off my property." Unknown to the woman, the path on which she was riding crossed the owner's private property. When the woman explained that she thought the path was a public trail, the owner cursed her, approached her horse, and struck the horse with his stick. As a result of the blow, the horse reared, causing the woman to fear that she would fall. However, the woman managed to stay on her horse, and then departed. Neither the woman nor the horse suffered bodily harm.
In an action against the owner for damages, will the woman likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the owner was privileged to exclude trespassers from his property.
choices.B: No, because the woman suffered no physical harm.
choices.C: Yes, for battery and assault.
choices.D: Yes, for trespass to chattels.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
Battery v. Assault
Intentional act
(striking horse with stick)
Battery
Contact
harmful or offensive contact
(horse struck by stick)
Assault
Apprehension
apprehension of imminent contact
(fear of falling)

Battery occurs when:

  • the defendant intends to cause contact with the plaintiff's person
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct causes such contact and
  • that contact causes bodily harm or is offensive to the plaintiff.

Contact with the plaintiff's person encompasses contact with anything connected to the plaintiff's person. Therefore, the owner committed a battery when he intentionally struck the horse the woman was riding.

Assault occurs when:

  • the defendant intends to cause the plaintiff to anticipate an imminent, and harmful or offensive, contact with the plaintiff's person and
  • the defendant's affirmative conduct causes the plaintiff to anticipate such contact.

Here, the owner intentionally caused the woman to anticipate imminent, harmful contact (fear of falling) when he struck her horse, so the owner committed an assault. And though a plaintiff cannot recover twice for the same harm (i.e., no double recovery), the owner's act of striking the horse caused the woman two distinct harms-contact and apprehension. Therefore, she can recover for battery AND assault.

(Choice A) A landowner is privileged to use reasonable force to stop an unexcused trespass if the landowner (1) first asks the trespasser to leave and (2) reasonably believes that force is necessary to remove the trespasser. Here, the owner told the woman to get off his property, but there is no evidence that force was necessary to remove her (e.g., had he told the owner she was staying).

(Choice B) The harm requirements for battery (harmful or offensive contact) and assault (apprehension of contact) can be satisfied without proof of bodily harm. Therefore, the woman's lack of physical harm will not prevent her from recovering damages.

(Choice D) Trespass to chattels by intentional intermeddling with another's possession of tangible property requires proof of actual damages-e.g., impairment of the physical condition or value of the chattel. But here, there is no evidence that the woman's horse was impaired-e.g., unable to walk.

📌 Educational Objective

Battery requires that the defendant's affirmative conduct cause harmful or offensive contact, while assault requires the defendant's affirmative conduct cause anticipation of such contact.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 101 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (listing the requirements for battery).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 105 (Am. L. Inst., Tentative Draft No. 1, 2015) (listing the requirements for assault).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子在她认为的公共小径上骑马时，小径旁一所房屋的所有权人一边挥舞着棍子一边走近她，并大喊：“离开我的地盘。”该女子不知道的是，她所骑行的小径穿过了该所有权人的私人土地。当该女子解释说她以为那是一条公共步道时，所有权人咒骂她，走近她的马，并用棍子击打了马匹。由于这一击打，马匹受惊后腿直立，导致该女子担心自己会摔下来。然而，该女子设法稳住了身子，没有从马上摔下来，然后离开了。该女子和马匹均未遭受身体伤害。

在向该所有权人提起的损害赔偿诉讼中，该女子是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为所有权人有权将非法侵入者驱逐出其财产范围。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该女子没有遭受身体伤害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为构成了伤害罪（battery）和侵犯（assault）。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为构成了动产侵权（trespass to chattels）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Intentional Torts - Battery

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：battery（电池） 和 assault（袭击） 是否都成立，关键看打到马是否算打到“人”，以及让她害怕摔下是否已构成可诉的即时恐惧。

三秒认题路径：

打马 → 算接触 → 造成恐惧 → battery + assault → 选 C

核心法律规则

battery（殴打） 要求被告故意造成对原告身体的有害或冒犯性接触，考场意思：不一定要把人打伤，碰到和人紧密相连的东西也可能算。

assault（袭击） 要求被告故意让原告预期即将发生的有害或冒犯性接触，考场意思：重点是她当下有没有“马上会被碰到”的 डर，不是事后有没有流血。

本题里，被告明知她骑在马上，还故意用棍子打马，既造成了接触，也让她担心自己会摔下，所以两项侵权都可能成立。

核心判例： Restatement 规则对应本题：接触到与人紧密连接的马，通常可算对人的接触；同一行为还能同时制造即时恐惧。

思维导图

先看被告做了什么：故意挥棍打马
Battery 关卡：接触到的不只是“马”，而是骑在上面的人所紧密连接的载体 → 这可算对人之接触
Assault 关卡：马被打后突然受惊，原告立刻担心自己会摔下 → 已形成即将发生接触的恐惧
卡死点：不要求身体受伤；physical harm 缺席也不妨碍成立
答案落点：同一动作制造两种独立损害 → 可同时主张 battery（殴打） + assault（袭击） → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她和马都没受伤，所以只能判没有赔偿。

但考试真正问的是：被告有没有造成法律上可认定的接触和即时恐惧，不是有没有留下肉眼可见伤痕。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另外，地主权利不是无限大；就算能赶走 trespasser，也要符合“先要求离开 + 需要合理用力”的条件，不能直接拿它当打人的通行证。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 故意打马 既让马与原告发生可归责接触，也让原告担心自己会摔下，所以 battery（殴打） 和 assault（袭击） 都能成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 保护权利过度

✕ A: 把 exclude trespassers 当成打人的免责条款了。

❌ 事实误判 | 把伤害看窄

✕ B: 只盯着 physical harm，忽略了接触和恐惧本身就够了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 侵权类型错位

✕ D: 把 trespass to chattels 套进来，但题目核心是打到人，不是单纯损坏马。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“打到谁”再抓“怕什么”，最后分别对照 battery（殴打） 与 assault（袭击）。

考场速记

记住：battery（殴打） 看接触，assault（袭击） 看即时恐惧；打到人骑的马，常常就是在打人。

速记口诀：“碰到人连着的东西，常算碰到人；让她怕立刻出事，常算 assault。”

reason.en: Sets up the owner's privilege-to-exclude defense in choice A.
reason.zh: 引出選項A中土地所有人驅離侵入者的特權抗辯。

reason.en: Establishes assault by imminent harmful contact with her person.

keywords.text: Neither the woman nor the horse suffered bodily harm

reason.en: Distracts test-takers toward choice B but does not defeat battery or assault.

reason.en: Intentional offensive contact with the horse satisfies battery against the rider.
reason.zh: 故意以冒犯方式击打所骑马匹，对骑手成立 battery。

highlights.text: Neither the woman nor the horse suffered bodily harm

reason.en: Lack of injury does not bar recovery because offensive contact and apprehension suffice.
reason.zh: 无伤害不妨碍求偿，冒犯性接觸与 apprehension 已足。

highlights.text: the path on which she was riding crossed the owner's private property

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A tile contractor was hired to install ceiling tiles in a new, multi-story office building. To speed up the installation process, the tile contractor rented scissor lifts from an equipment rental company. A sprinkler-system contractor who was also working on the building owned several identical scissor lifts that he was using to install sprinkler systems in the ceiling of each of the building's floors. The tile contractor mistakenly directed one of his employees to the wrong floor to retrieve the scissor lift from that floor. Consequently, the employee retrieved one of the lifts owned by the sprinkler-system contractor. The tile contractor used the lift for more than two weeks before the sprinkler-system contractor found and regained possession of the lift. The lift was in the same condition as when the tile contractor had taken it.
The sprinkler-system contractor sued the tile contractor for trespass to chattels, and the tile contractor defended on the basis that his taking and use of the lift was a reasonable mistake.
For whom is the court likely to rule?

choices.A: For the sprinkler-system contractor, because a reasonable mistake is no defense to a trespass-to-chattels action.
choices.B: For the sprinkler-system contractor, because the tile contractor's mistake was not a mistake of law.
choices.C: For the tile contractor, because the condition of the lift had not been changed by his actions.
choices.D: For the tile contractor, because the sprinkler-system contractor's lift was identical to the ones rented by the tile contractor.

questions.explanation:
Trespass to chattels
Plaintiff has possession or immediate right to possession of chattel
↓
Defendant intentionally interferes with possession through either:
Dispossession
↓
Harm inferred
Use or intermeddling
↓
Causes harm
  • actual harm to chattel
  • substantial loss of use of chattel or
  • bodily harm to plaintiff

Trespass to chattels (ie, tangible personal property) occurs when the defendant intentionally interferes with the plaintiff's possessory rights by either:

• dispossessing the plaintiff of the chattel or
• using or intermeddling with the plaintiff's chattel.

Only the intent to do the interfering act is necessary. Therefore, the defendant's belief, because of a mistake of law or fact, that he/she was privileged to act is no defense to a trespass-to-chattels action (Choice B). This is true even if the mistake was reasonable.

Here, the tile contractor intentionally dispossessed the sprinkler-system contractor of his scissor lift for more than two weeks. The tile contractor's apparent belief that the lift taken was one of the lifts he had rented (mistake of fact) is no defense—no matter how reasonable that mistake may have been given that the lifts were identical (Choice D). For this reason, the court will likely rule for the sprinkler-system contractor.

Choice C) In cases of dispossession (as here seen), the plaintiff can recover for loss of use of the chattel without proof of actual harm (eg, damage to the chattel). Therefore, the tile contractor can be liable to the sprinkler-system contractor even though the tile contractor's actions had not changed the condition of the lift.

📌 Educational Objective

Trespass to chattels is an intentional interference with another's tangible personal property through dispossession, use, or intermeddling. The defendant's erroneous belief, because of a mistake of fact or law, that he/she was privileged to do the interfering act is no defense.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Torts § 244 (Am. Law Inst. 1965) (effect of mistake on trespass to chattels).
questions.zh-question:
一名瓷砖承包商受雇为一栋新建的多层办公楼安装天花板瓷砖。为了加快安装过程，该瓷砖承包商从一家设备租赁公司租用了剪式升降机。另一名同样在该大楼工作的消防喷淋系统承包商拥有几台相同的剪式升降机，他正用这些升降机在每层楼的天花板上安装消防喷淋系统。瓷砖承包商错误地指示其一名员工去错误的楼层取回那里的剪式升降机。结果，该员工取走了一台属于消防喷淋系统承包商的升降机。在消防喷淋系统承包商发现并收回该升降机之前，瓷砖承包商使用了它超过两周。升降机的状况与瓷砖承包商取走时相同。

消防喷淋系统承包商以侵犯动产（trespass to chattels）为由起诉瓷砖承包商，而瓷砖承包商则以其取用升降机是合理错误为由进行辩护。

法院可能支持哪一方？

zh-choices.A: 支持消防喷淋系统承包商，因为合理错误不能作为对侵犯动产（trespass to chattels）诉讼的抗辩理由。
zh-choices.B: 支持消防喷淋系统承包商，因为瓷砖承包商的错误并非法律上的错误。
zh-choices.C: 支持瓷砖承包商，因为其行为未改变升降机的状况。
zh-choices.D: 支持瓷砖承包商，因为消防喷淋系统承包商的升降机与瓷砖承包商租用的升降机完全相同。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Intentional Torts - Trespass to chattels

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告把别人的动产拿走并使用时，故意实施干涉（intentional interference）就够了；即使他是合理误认（reasonable mistake），也不是抗辩。

三秒认题路径：

动产被拿走 → 故意干涉 → 误认不是抗辩 → 看是否贬损/丧失使用 → 原告赢

核心法律规则

侵害动产（trespass to chattels）是对他人有形动产的故意干涉，方式可以是剥夺占有（dispossession），也可以是使用或插手（use or intermeddling）。考场意思：只要你是故意拿、故意用、故意碰，就先进门。

这里不要求被告知道那件东西一定是别人的；他对事实误认（mistake of fact）或法律误认（mistake of law），都不能把故意干涉变成无责任。考场意思：reasonable 也没用，错拿了还是错拿了。

如果是剥夺占有（dispossession），原告可以直接主张使用损失（loss of use），不必先证明物件被弄坏。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Torts § 244 - 误认有无授权，不会替你挡掉侵害动产责任。

思维导图

先看：被告有没有故意干涉他人的有形动产？
YES：这里是把对方的 scissor lift 拿走并用了两周，已经进入 trespass to chattels。
再看抗辩：他主张“我只是拿错了，还是合理的”。
卡死点：reasonable mistake 不是抗辩；故意干涉已经成立。
最后看损害：这题是 dispossession，所以即使 lift 没坏，loss of use 也足够。
结论：法院会判给 sprinkler-system contractor。对应正确选项 A。
NO：如果只是无意碰到、也没有占有或使用，就不进这个规则。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 lift 完全没坏，而且还是拿去和自家设备长得一模一样的东西，应该不算侵权。

但考试真正问的是：被告有没有故意干涉他人占有，不是他主观上有没有“说得通的理由”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题最常见的错觉就是把“没损坏”当成“没责任”；其实被剥夺使用两周，本身就够了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键事实是：tile contractor 拿走并使用了两周，已经是故意干涉占有；reasonable mistake 不会洗掉 trespass to chattels 责任。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把 mistake of law 当成唯一死穴，想太窄了。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ C: 盯着“没坏”就放人，忽略了 loss of use。

❌ 事实误判 | 相同设备偷换

✕ D: 看到“长得一样”就以为可拿错，题目要的是占有被故意干涉。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓行为类型，再问误认能不能抗辩；本题直接用“故意干涉 + 误认无效 + 失去使用即可”三步锁答案。

考场速记

记住一句话：侵害动产（trespass to chattels）看的是“你故意碰没碰、拿没拿、用没用”，不是你觉得自己有没有理由。

速记：intentional interference 成立后，mistake 不救你；dispossession 还会直接带出 loss of use。

questions.subject: Torts
questions.question:
A college student and her roommate were invited to a Halloween party. The roommate decided to dress up as an anime character whose defining feature was bright green hair. The roommate planned to buy a wig, but the student convinced the roommate to allow the student to dye the roommate's hair using a temporary green dye that would wash out after a single shampoo. They went to a store where the roommate accidentally purchased a bottle of permanent dye. The student noticed that the dye was permanent but did not point out the roommate's mistake. Instead, the student applied the permanent, bright-green dye to the roommate's hair. Unable to dye her hair back in time for her next shift, the roommate lost her part-time job as a server.
If the roommate sues the student for battery, is the roommate likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the roommate consented to having her hair dyed by the student.
choices.B: No, because the student did not misrepresent the permanent nature of the dye.
choices.C: Yes, because the roommate lost her part-time job as a server.
choices.D: Yes, because the student was aware of the roommate's mistake.

questions.explanation:
Negation of actual consent
Lack of capacity
  • Plaintiff’s lack of capacity due to youth, intoxication, or intellectual incompetence may negate validity of consent
  • Plaintiff who appreciates nature, extent & potential consequences of defendant’s conduct has capacity to consent to it
  • Adult generally is rebuttably presumed to have capacity to consent
Duress
  • Actual consent given under duress (e.g., physical force, threats) is not valid
  • Threat must be of present action, not future action
  • Threats of economic duress & moral pressure generally do not render plaintiff’s consent invalid
Substantial mistake
  • Actual consent due to substantial mistake regarding nature of invasion of plaintiff’s interests, extent of expected harm, or defendant’s purpose in engaging in conduct is vitiated as defendant:
    • caused mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or
    • knew of mistake

When a defendant intends to cause contact with the plaintiff’s person, the defendant causes such contact, and that contact is harmful or offensive to the plaintiff, the defendant is liable for battery absent a defense. Actual consent is a defense to battery (and other intentional torts) when (1) the plaintiff is willing for the defendant’s contact to occur and (2) that conduct is within the scope of the plaintiff’s consent. And actual consent is valid despite the plaintiff’s substantial mistake regarding the nature of the invasion of his/her interests unless the defendant:

  • caused the mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or
  • knew about the mistake.

Here, the student applied permanent, bright-green dye to the roommate’s hair (harmful contact). Although the roommate consented to having her hair dyed by the student, the roommate believed that the dye she had purchased was temporary (substantial mistake) (Choice A). The student was aware of the roommate’s mistake but said nothing. Therefore, the roommate’s consent is no defense, and the roommate will likely prevail in her suit against the student for battery.

(Choice B) Although the student did not misrepresent the permanent nature of the dye, the student knew that the roommate mistakenly believed it was temporary. This is enough to render the roommate’s consent invalid.

(Choice C) Battery does not require proof of actual harm, so evidence that the roommate lost her job does not provide a basis for her to prevail. Instead, this evidence goes to how much she can recover in damages once her battery claim is established.

📌 Educational Objective

Actual consent to a contact is valid despite the plaintiff’s substantial mistake regarding the nature of the invasion of his/her interests unless the defendant (1) caused the mistake by affirmative misrepresentation or fraud or (2) knew about the mistake.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 13 (Am. L. Inst. Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (defining actual consent).
  • Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 15 (Am. L. Inst. Tentative Draft No. 4, 2019) (setting forth how actual consent can be negated by substantial mistake).
questions.zh-question:
一名大学生和她的室友被邀请参加一个万圣节派对。室友决定装扮成一个动漫角色，其标志性特征是亮绿色的头发。室友本打算买一顶假发，但该学生说服室友让她用一种一次性洗发水就能洗掉的临时绿色染发剂为室友染发。她们去了一家商店，室友在那里意外地购买了一瓶永久性染发剂。该学生注意到染发剂是永久性的，但没有指出室友的错误。相反，该学生将永久性的亮绿色染发剂用在了室友的头发上。由于无法在下次轮班前将头发染回原色，室友失去了她作为服务员的兼职工作。

如果室友以伤害罪（battery）起诉该学生，室友是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为室友同意该学生为她染发。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该学生没有歪曲染发剂的永久性质。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为室友失去了她作为服务员的兼职工作。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该学生知晓室友的错误。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Torts: Intentional Torts - Consent

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：实际同意（actual consent）遇到重大误解时，只有在被告知道或诱发该误解时，才会被打掉。

三秒认题路径：

先有同意 → 但有误解 → 被告知道 → 同意失效 → 电池成立

核心法律规则

抓住这一条就够了

battery（殴打侵权）里，actual consent（实际同意）通常可以抗辩，但同意必须是“知道自己在同意什么”。

如果原告对接触的性质有substantial mistake（重大误解），而被告要么用fraud（欺骗）诱发误解，要么明知对方误解却不纠正，这个同意就失效。

所以这题的关键不是“她愿不愿意染头发”，而是“她愿不愿意被染成永久的绿色”；被告明知她以为是临时染剂，仍然下手，抗辩被打掉。

核心判例： Restatement (Third) of Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons § 15 - 这条规则直接锁定：重大误解只有在被告知道或制造时，才会让同意失效。

思维导图

先看：受害人有没有给过同意？
有 但她同意的是“temporary dye（临时染剂）”，不是永久染发。
再看：这个误解是不是substantial mistake（重大误解）？
是 误解正好打在接触性质上，属于会影响是否同意的那种。
最后一关：被告有没有知道误解还照做？
有 于是同意失效，结论直接走向：选 D，原告更可能胜诉

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她明明自己答应了染头发，所以学生一定有抗辩。

但考试真正问的是：她答应的是“临时变装”，不是“永久改色”；被告又明知她搞错了还继续染，这就把同意打穿了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干关键点是：学生明知对方以为是 temporary dye，却仍改用 permanent dye；这种重大误解下的同意会失效，所以电池成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只看表面同意

✕ A: 把“同意染发”误当成“同意永久染发”。

❌ 法律适用 | 误把欺骗当唯一条件

✕ B: 误以为没直接撒谎就没事，但 knew of the mistake 也足够。

❌ 事实误判 | 把损害当要件

✕ C: 把失去工作当成是否成立电池的门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“同意是否有效”，再查有没有重大误解和被告知情。

考场速记

记住一句：actual consent 不是“点头就行”，而是“知道自己同意的是哪一种接触”。

看到“我以为是临时、他却明知是永久”这种题，先想：substantial mistake + 被告知情 = 同意失效。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Apply consent defense exceptions to battery

reason.en: Defines the nature and extent of contact the roommate believed she consented to.
reason.zh: 界定室友认为自己同意的接触性质与范围。

reason.en: The actual invasion differed from what the roommate understood she was authorizing.
reason.zh: 实际侵害与室友理解的授权内容不同。

keywords.text: did not point out the roommate's mistake

reason.en: Student's awareness of the mistake can vitiate consent even without affirmative misrepresentation.
reason.zh: 被告知晓错误可在无积极虚假陈述时仍使同意无效。

reason.en: Frames the claim and triggers analysis of whether valid consent is a defense.
reason.zh: 框定诉讼请求并触发对有效同意是否构成抗辩的分析。

keywords.text: convinced the roommate to allow the student to dye

reason.en: Shows the roommate initially authorized contact, setting up the consent defense issue.
reason.zh: 表明室友最初授权接触，从而引出同意抗辩问题。

A.text: consented to having her hair dyed

reason.en: Ignores that consent is invalid when the defendant knows of a substantial mistake about the invasion.
reason.zh: 忽视被告知晓关于侵害性质的重大错误时同意无效。

B.text: did not misrepresent the permanent nature of the dye

reason.en: Confuses the need for affirmative fraud with the separate rule that knowledge of mistake suffices.
reason.zh: 混淆积极欺诈要件与知晓错误即可使同意无效的规则。

C.text: lost her part-time job as a server

reason.en: Battery liability does not depend on proof of actual harm such as job loss.
reason.zh: 殴打责任不取决于失业等实际损害的证明。

reason.en: Directly states the exception that defeats the consent defense here.
reason.zh: 直接指出在此情形下否定同意抗辩的例外。

highlights.text: temporary green dye that would wash out after a single shampoo

label.zh: 关于侵害性质的重大错误

reason.en: Shows the roommate consented only to temporary dyeing, not permanent alteration.
reason.zh: 表明室友仅同意临时染发，而非永久性改变。

highlights.text: The student noticed that the dye was permanent but did not point out the roommate's mistake.

reason.en: This fact triggers the rule that known mistake renders consent ineffective.
reason.zh: 该事实触发知晓错误则同意无效的规则。

highlights.text: If the roommate sues the student for battery

reason.en: Poses whether intentional hair dyeing is actionable battery despite initial permission.
reason.zh: 提出在最初许可下故意染发是否构成可诉的殴打。

highlights.text: accidentally purchased a bottle of permanent dye

reason.en: Creates the substantial mistake about the nature and extent of the expected contact.
reason.zh: 造成对预期接触性质与范围的重大错误。
